one_line: A portfolio that exposes verified candidate facts and role-specific matching to browser agents.
what_it_does: Lets recruiters' agents retrieve structured portfolio evidence, score a role, tailor the view, and generate a targeted resume.
leverage_rationale: Typed, shared page state and deterministic matching improve reliability over scraping, but a general agent could obtain much of the same result from a portfolio UI with friction.
leverage_evidence: 11 typed WebMCP tools are described, including get_evidence and match_role.
The page visibly reshapes and renders fit results from agent actions per the submission description.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent, broad feature set and live demo, but no video or transcript is supplied and the underlying portfolio predates the submission.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and public repository are reported.
Submission claims the WebMCP surfaces, scoring engine, and resume flow were added during the period.
impact_rationale: Recruiters and candidates have a concrete matching and evidence-verification problem; the proposed workflow addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Role-specific fit, gaps, evidence verification, and resume generation target recruiter screening.
Pitch identifies agent scraping and short recruiter attention as the problem.
creativity_rationale: A portfolio that collaborates with an agent and adapts itself live is a fresh synthesis with a purposeful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent brings the role while the site supplies verified candidate facts.
Tailoring the live portfolio and generating a role-targeted resume extend beyond static portfolio presentation.
usability_note: The described one-page flow is understandable, though evidence is packaging-only.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; visual claims cannot be independently checked.
standouts: Strong alignment between structured candidate evidence and recruiter intent.
advance_reason: Credible concept and meaningful agent-facing workflow; merits further review despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: A WebMCP scheduling sandbox where agents optimize a factory draft while humans retain commit authority.
what_it_does: Models an automotive paint line, exposes stable state and constraints, optimizes isolated schedules, compares revisions, and requests approval.
leverage_rationale: The agent must reason over structured, stateful constraints and alternatives; WebMCP materially improves precision and preserves a human approval boundary.
leverage_evidence: Tools inspect machines, orders, calendars, constraints, drafts, and committed revisions.
Only a human click can commit; protected orders and overtime limits are enforced by the engine.
execution_rationale: The workflow and safety boundary are unusually coherent, but no video/transcript is supplied and the packet is primarily self-claim.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and public repository reported.
Description specifies isolated draft, deterministic optimizer, baseline comparison, and review request.
impact_rationale: Production scheduling has a real operational audience and costly constraint errors; the human-in-the-loop design addresses a credible need.
impact_evidence: Synthetic factory scenario reports fewer paint changes, fewer late orders, and more on-time orders.
Explicit distinction between agent analysis and human authorization.
creativity_rationale: The constrained draft-versus-committed scheduling collaboration is a strong, purposeful application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Safety boundary is implemented as product behavior rather than prompt text.
Agent explores alternatives without silently mutating the production plan.
usability_note: The staged workflow appears clear for its operational simulation.
red_flags: No video evidence; end-to-end completion is not observed.
standouts: Strong state and approval model for consequential scheduling changes.
advance_reason: High WebMCP relevance and credible operational value justify advancement.

one_line: A workspace that turns a user's demonstrated routine into a reusable WebMCP tool.
what_it_does: Records semantic commands from a manual triage routine, has an agent parameterize them, and registers the resulting tool into the live page.
leverage_rationale: The core product is user-created agent capability grounded in live page state; reproducing this without structured tools would require coding or brittle UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Teach records commands in an application vocabulary rather than clicks or screen positions.
Agent proposes a named, parameterized tool and the page gains it at runtime.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent and detailed, but the packet lacks video/transcript and only claims the central flow.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete 1000-story triage scenario and four recorded commands.
demo_alive=alive and public repository reported.
impact_rationale: Non-programmers who repeat cross-tab routines have a real automation gap, and teaching by demonstration directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Dentist SEO triage story identifies recurring manual switching costs.
Concrete filter/tag/priority routine is converted into reusable automation.
creativity_rationale: Runtime creation of WebMCP tools from demonstrations is a genuinely novel interaction model and ambitious hackathon concept.
creativity_evidence: The user grows the tool surface instead of a developer writing each integration.
Semantic routine capture plus agent-generated parameters is memorable and distinctive.
usability_note: Teaching by doing is accessible in principle; generated-tool review details are not evidenced.
red_flags: No video or transcript; runtime registration and repeat execution remain unverified.
standouts: Most original interaction model in the packet.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and strong WebMCP delta warrant advancement, pending execution verification.

one_line: A private in-browser CSV cleaning workbench where agents propose diffs and humans approve writes.
what_it_does: Profiles and analyzes local CSV data, charts problems, proposes exact before/after changes, and requires human approval for every mutation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to the same local object as the UI while preserving privacy and explicit write approval; a server or UI-driving agent is materially inferior.
leverage_evidence: File remains in the browser; tools operate on the same JavaScript object rendered by the UI.
Writes are diffs requiring an Approve/Reject click and no tool mutates the table.
execution_rationale: The safety and data-flow design is internally consistent, though no video/transcript is available to demonstrate the complete flow.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and public repository reported.
Description specifies profiling, queries/charts, diff cards, approval, and privacy receipt.
impact_rationale: Analysts have a common, costly data-cleaning problem and privacy constraints; local agent assistance with review directly addresses both.
impact_evidence: Concrete CSV issues include inconsistent regions, currency, dates, and duplicates.
Zero-upload design targets sensitive customer and salary data.
creativity_rationale: The reads-free/writes-as-proposals rule is a compelling interaction and safety model for agentic data work.
creativity_evidence: Privacy receipt and shared local state make the design more than a generic cleaner.
Deliberately withholding undo from tools keeps reversal with the human.
usability_note: Diff review and explicit approval are legible and trust-building.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; claims about local-only processing are not visually verified.
advance_reason: High-value, highly WebMCP-native workflow with strong safety design.

one_line: A renovation operations dashboard that exposes assignment and spatial room context to agents.
what_it_does: Answers product questions from assignment, address, room, and resident-choice data, visualizes the selected room, and stages approved operational actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to deep operational and spatial context is useful, but the described lookup and proposal flows could be partly reproduced through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP reads selected assignment, address, room, and catalog data.
Actions require explicit human approval before write-back.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent integrated demo, but there is no video/transcript and no public repository to inspect.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive reported.
Description names dashboard, chat, execution map, and 3D building/room view.
impact_rationale: Contractors and renovation operators have real information-retrieval and coordination needs; exact room-specific product answers are useful.
impact_evidence: Concrete shower-mixer lookup scenario.
Operational action proposals preserve source-of-truth ownership.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent queries with spatial 3D room context is a fresh application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: The workflow connects structured dashboard data to selectable building and bathroom context.
Human-approved operational actions are integrated into the same experience.
usability_note: Many surfaces may create interaction complexity; visual evidence was unavailable.
red_flags: No public repo and no video evidence; 3D and agent workflow claims are unverified.
standouts: Agent answer linked to spatial room context rather than generic text search.
advance_reason: Credible enterprise workflow, though evidence is thin.

one_line: A wallet copilot that audits approvals and stages transactions while only the wallet signs.
what_it_does: Scans and explains token approvals, researches tokens, quarantines injection content, and stages revokes/transfers/swaps for wallet confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Browser-local wallet signing and shared page state create a meaningful capability and security boundary that a general agent cannot safely complete remotely.
leverage_evidence: stage_revoke returns awaiting_user_confirmation and cannot click the wallet popup.
Tools combine approval scanning, risk explanation, token assessment, and staged actions.
execution_rationale: The security model is coherent and detailed, but the packet has no video/transcript and live wallet behavior is not observed.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and public repository reported.
Description details scan, explain, assess, and staged transaction flows.
impact_rationale: Wallet approval risk is a high-stakes problem for crypto users, and the product addresses it without delegating private-key authority.
impact_evidence: Concrete approval-drain problem and explainable risk scoring.
Human-only signing is retained for revokes, transfers, and swaps.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-auditor/stager, wallet-as-signer split is a strong security-aware interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Injection quarantine is treated as part of the product boundary.
Agent can research and prepare actions without access to keys.
usability_note: Conversation-based audit is promising, but transaction review UX is unverified.
red_flags: No video evidence; security claims and wallet confirmation behavior need observation.
standouts: Clear zero-delegation safety principle for consequential actions.
advance_reason: High-impact security workflow with strong WebMCP rationale.

one_line: A food-verification layer that returns sourced allergy and nutrition verdicts or refuses to guess.
what_it_does: Accepts household constraints, checks products or menus against an evidence corpus, returns dated source-backed verdicts, and logs agent activity visibly.
leverage_rationale: Structured, evidence-bearing verdicts and honest refusal make the agent interaction substantially more reliable than browsing labels ad hoc, while WebMCP exposes the live ledger to the human.
leverage_evidence: Four explicit verdict states include ask-one-question and couldn't-verify.
Every verdict carries source and read date; WebMCP actions appear in a visible ledger.
execution_rationale: The submission presents a coherent multi-surface system and measured claims, but lacks video/transcript evidence for the actual product flow.
execution_evidence: Hosted MCP, WebMCP, and REST surfaces share a ruling engine per description.
Claimed production comparison resolves a question in two API calls under five seconds.
impact_rationale: Families managing allergies and nutrition have a specific high-consequence information need; sourced refusal is valuable when evidence is incomplete.
impact_evidence: Concrete milk-allergy restaurant question.
System avoids the word safe and treats unknown as requiring no unsupported verdict.
creativity_rationale: Treating refusal, provenance, and read date as first-class product outputs is a thoughtful and memorable agent interaction.
creativity_evidence: Evidence-backed ruling model spans hosted MCP, WebMCP, and REST.
Public refusal metrics reinforce the epistemic design.
usability_note: The small verdict vocabulary and visible evidence are user-friendly in principle.
red_flags: Health-adjacent claims and production performance are not visually verified in this packet.
standouts: Strong refusal and provenance design for a high-stakes question.
advance_reason: Clear audience, high consequence value, and disciplined evidence model.

one_line: An identity, reputation, and audit layer for agents interacting with websites.
what_it_does: Authenticates agents via email OTP, records tool calls as audit events, and adjusts interaction limits based on accumulated reputation.
leverage_rationale: Structured identity and audit state can improve agent access control, but the packet does not establish that WebMCP itself is indispensable versus a conventional service API.
leverage_evidence: AuditEvent includes agent identity, tool, result, reputation delta, and resulting score.
OTP handshake and reputation-dependent limits are described as WebMCP interactions.
execution_rationale: The description is incomplete and no frame sheets or video are submitted; the central authentication flow is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: FACTS report demo_alive=alive but no public repository.
Packet supplies only a packaging screenshot and prose fragment.
impact_rationale: Websites and legitimate agents have a real trust and bot-mitigation problem, and auditable differentiated access is a credible response.
impact_evidence: Identified tension between bot defenses and legitimate delegated agents.
Reputation history supports differentiated limits rather than a single generic rate limit.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent identity, reputation deltas, and OTP is useful infrastructure, though familiar trust-system components are not deeply evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Agent-specific auditable interaction history is the core proposal.
Reputation changes are tied to individual tool outcomes.
usability_note: OTP for an agent-mediated session may be workable, but the flow is not shown.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video; prose is truncated and execution evidence is especially thin.
standouts: Attempts to make agent trust and auditability first-class site capabilities.
advance_reason: Potentially useful infrastructure, but the packet does not demonstrate enough of the product to advance confidently.

one_line: A restaurant floor and queue simulator where an agent plans seating and a host retains control.
what_it_does: Simulates a five-hour service, exposes floor/queue state through WebMCP, lets agents optimize seating under rules, and supports human accept/reject/override.
leverage_rationale: An agent must reason over shared, changing floor state and many hard constraints; 22 structured tools are more reliable than driving a drag-and-drop UI.
leverage_evidence: Human and agent share floor, clock, queue, and version number.
Engine enforces capacity, accessibility, high chairs, locks, timers, and reservation priority while agent optimizes preferences.
execution_rationale: The 96-second video transcript explicitly describes the central simulator, agent hookup, and automatic reservation planning; the packet presents a coherent scoped product.
execution_evidence: Video transcript describes simulator state and agent planning all reservations onto tables.
Product defines one-screen floor, queue, five-hour service, and human override flow.
impact_rationale: Restaurant hosts face a real multi-variable allocation problem, and better waits and utilization are credible benefits even in a simulation.
impact_evidence: Transcript identifies manual assignment inefficiency.
Description targets customer satisfaction, table turn rate, revenue, and fair allocation of scarce tables.
creativity_rationale: The shared-floor collaboration and explicit division between hard rules, agent judgment, and host authority is an original, well-pursued framing.
creativity_evidence: Agent explains choices while host can reject with a reason or override by hand.
Live restaurant simulator makes the optimization interaction tangible.
usability_note: Single-screen floor and queue with human overrides is a clear operational model.
standouts: Strong end-to-end video evidence and clear human/agent division of labor.
advance_reason: Demonstrated central workflow, high leverage, and credible operational value.

one_line: A browser-boundary debugger that turns postMessage failures into evidence, contracts, and verified repairs.
what_it_does: Reproduces iframe lifecycle, protocol, and identity failures; records boundary evidence; lets an agent stage a report-only contract for human review and verification.
leverage_rationale: The live browser boundary is the evidence source and shared workspace; structured WebMCP access makes precise diagnosis and reviewed repair possible where logs and UI scraping are inadequate.
leverage_evidence: Records timing, origin, WindowProxy/source identity, protocol, policy verdict, and rendered result.
Agent can inspect developer-selected incidents and stage the smallest evidence-justified contract.
execution_rationale: The packet describes four deterministic scenarios and verified outcomes, with a 175-second product video reported, though no transcript is included.
execution_evidence: Verified repair preserves $120; broken same-origin sibling changes it to $0.01 and fails three checks.
Scenario lab covers lifecycle race, protocol drift, wrong frame identity, and evidence-dependent diagnosis.
impact_rationale: postMessage failures affect payments, authentication, editors, widgets, and microfrontends; precise shared evidence can materially shorten debugging.
impact_evidence: Concrete checkout integrity scenario and preserved $120 result.
Targets failure causes ordinary logs often omit: timing, origin, source identity, and protocol.
creativity_rationale: Making the live browser security boundary a collaborative debugging instrument is a genuinely novel and technically ambitious interaction.
creativity_evidence: Controlled failures change diagnosis based on selected evidence.
Human-reviewed contracts plus verified repair connect diagnosis to a bounded fix.
usability_note: Evidence selection and report-only repair are appropriate for developers, though the workflow is specialized.
red_flags: Video transcript excerpt is absent, so agent invocation details rely on description.
standouts: Strong technical specificity and unusually compelling browser-native debugging use case.
advance_reason: High leverage and creativity with concrete failure/repair evidence; advance.
